Grannos.json.text: Grannos, also spelled Grannus, is a Gaulish healing god whom Roman worshippers joined to Apollo. The pairing belongs to interpretatio romana, the habit of matching Celtic gods with Greek and Roman ones. He governed healing waters across Europe and Scotland, and his cult was shared with the goddess Sirona, whose name means something like 'star goddess'. Eighteen inscriptions name him. Only one, from Bonn, calls him Grannus alone. Elsewhere the name serves as a byname of Apollo. Offerings appear in the Rhineland, at Musselburgh near Edinburgh, at Brigetio in Hungary, at Astorga in Spain, in Västmanland in Sweden, and at Ephesus in Turkey. Aachen was known as Aquis Granni, 'the waters of Grannus', which points to a sacred spring. His name seems to spring from the same root as Grian, the Irish sun figure, and the heroine Gráinne has been proposed as a further cognate. In the Auvergne, worshippers set grain sheaves on fire and sang to him as friend, father, and mother, a sign of a dual or unclear gender.

Glewlwyd_Gafaelwar.json.text: Glewlwyd Gafaelwar is a Welsh hero and guardian figure who became the gatekeeper of Arthur's court. The oldest text that names him is a dialogue poem that asks, 'Who is the gatekeeper?' (Pa Gur yv y Porthaur?). There he stubbornly refuses entry to Arthur, Cai, and a crowd of the best men in the world. In Culhwch ac Olwen his role reverses. He bars the gate of Arthur's court at Celliwig against Culhwch, then goes inside and praises the young man to Arthur in a long and boastful speech. The poem hints that he held the gate only on three high festivals, with deputies at other times. His epithet suggests that guarding the gate was his fixed office. Some tellings place Arthur's court at Camelot rather than Celliwig. He does not appear in Chrétien de Troyes's Yvain or Erec et Enide, and his place in the Welsh romances marks a native figure pushing back into plots borrowed from French. His stand at the door has an Irish parallel: the gatekeeper Camall mac Rágail first denies Lug entry at Tara in Cath Maige Tuired.
